explanations.why: The proposed change starts from 1 working + 1 standby, which matches the 1W+1S in Part1.pdf, even though Part1.pdf says waste water instead of floor wash water. Part3.pdf and Part4.pdf both say 2W with no standby, which makes the exact baseline somewhat unclear.
explanations.consequence: If the wrong number of working pumps is built, the system may lack the needed pumping capacity or waste money and space on extra running equipment.

explanations.why: The proposed change explicitly states the starting arrangement is 1 working + 1 standby, matching the 1W+1S quote in Part1.pdf. However, Part3.pdf specifically names floor wash water transfer pumps and matches Part4.pdf at 2W, leaving some uncertainty.
explanations.consequence: Building the 2W arrangement instead of adding a standby pump leaves the plant with no backup pump if one fails, risking floor wash water overflow.
